key_insight: Sex was reported in 99.44% of trials, but gender in only 0.95%, revealing a major gap in characterizing participant representation.
clinical_relevance: Female participation below disease prevalence in 8 of 10 assessed conditions raises questions about how well trial populations represent affected populations.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 58,007 interventional trials with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
Examined trial characteristics associated with sex and gender reporting.
Compared female enrollment share with female disease prevalence using participation-to-prevalence ratios (PPRs).
evidence_signal: Across 16,097 trial–condition combinations, 43.0% achieved a PPR of at least 0.90; condition-level median PPRs ranged from 0.68 for COPD to 1.05 for obesity.
watch_item: Registry reporting may not reflect what trials actually collected, and these observational associations do not establish causality.
paper_title: Sex and Gender Reporting and Female Participation Relative to Disease Burden in ClinicalTrials.gov
